title: VPC Terraform modules (alpha) — module interface notes (draft)
content:
Context / goal
- Drafting the input/output contracts for the alpha Terraform module set used for Redwood Private (VPC) deployments.
- This is a working doc for ENG-4821. Expect churn. The intent is: stable-ish outputs for installer integration, while allowing customers to adopt pieces.

Owner notes (Bruno)
- I’m optimizing for:
  1) Minimal required inputs for a "golden path" deployment.
  2) Reasonable partial adoption (existing VPC / existing subnets).
  3) Outputs that map cleanly into redwood-private-installer networking config.
- Open questions are called out explicitly.

---

Early diagram (very rough)

  Customer account
  └─ VPC (10.x/16)
     ├─ Public subnets (optional; only if NAT/IGW enabled)
     │   └─ NAT GW (single or per-AZ)
     ├─ Private subnets (default for most workloads)
     │   ├─ Interface endpoints (ECR api/dkr, Logs, STS?, SSM?)
     │   └─ Redwood data plane components (varies; installer uses subnet IDs)
     └─ Isolated subnets (optional)
         └─ For strictly no-egress tiers / future use

Control plane / installer integration
- Installer requires a set of subnet IDs + endpoint reachability + DNS resolution.
- We should expose outputs that allow preflight checks to be deterministic (e.g., endpoint DNS enabled, route to S3 gateway present).

---

Repo structure (assumed)
- modules/
  - vpc-baseline
  - vpc-endpoints
  - security-groups-baseline
  - redwood-private-vpc (wrapper)

Naming conventions (proposed)
- Variables
  - Use snake_case.
  - Prefix with module context, but avoid redundant names when already in module.
  - All resources must be tagged with: env, owner, cost_center, data_class (per Infra tagging standard; confirm exact keys later).
- Outputs
  - Use snake_case.
  - Prefer stable, semantically named outputs over exposing raw resource IDs for everything.
  - Provide both "by AZ" (map/list) and "flat list" outputs where the installer may not care about AZ affinity.

Required common variables (across modules)
- name_prefix (string)
  - Used for naming resources: "redwood-private" / "acme-redwood" etc.
- env (string)
  - Ex: dev/stage/prod. Used in tags + name.
- tags (map(string))
  - Additional tags merged into required baseline.

---

Module: vpc-baseline

Purpose
- Create (or optionally reference) a VPC with subnet tiering, route tables, and optional NAT strategy.
- Opinionated defaults aligned with ADR-0127.

Modes
A) create mode (default)
- Creates VPC + subnets + route tables + IGW/NAT (depending on inputs).

B) existing VPC / existing subnets mode (partial adoption)
- VPC is provided (vpc_id) and/or subnet IDs are provided.
- Module should disable conflicting creation and validate that inputs are consistent.

Inputs (draft)
- create_vpc (bool, default true)
- vpc_id (string, optional; required when create_vpc=false)
- vpc_cidr (string, required when create_vpc=true)
- availability_zones (list(string), required)
  - Explicit list to avoid implicit provider ordering.

Subnet layout
- subnet_tiers (list(string), default ["public","private","isolated"])
  - NOTE: for alpha we may fix tiers to public/private/isolated to reduce variance.
- public_subnet_cidrs_by_az (map(string), optional)
- private_subnet_cidrs_by_az (map(string), optional)
- isolated_subnet_cidrs_by_az (map(string), optional)

Existing subnet adoption inputs
- public_subnet_ids (list(string), optional)
- private_subnet_ids (list(string), optional)
- isolated_subnet_ids (list(string), optional)

Egress / NAT
- enable_internet_gateway (bool, default false)
  - Default false for Private. If true, requires public subnets.
- nat_mode (string, default "none")
  - Allowed: none | single | per_az | centralized
  - "centralized" = use existing NAT/proxy (see ENG-4830; may be beta not alpha).
- existing_nat_gateway_ids_by_az (map(string), optional; only for nat_mode=centralized?)
- enable_dns_hostnames (bool, default true)
- enable_dns_support (bool, default true)

Flow logs (might live here OR separate module)
- enable_flow_logs (bool, default true)
- flow_logs_destination (string, default "cloudwatch")
  - Allowed: cloudwatch | s3
- flow_logs_retention_days (number, default 30)
  - CloudWatch only. For S3, require lifecycle policy outside scope? (maybe expose s3 lifecycle toggle).

Outputs (draft)
- vpc_id
- vpc_cidr
- availability_zones

Subnets
- public_subnet_ids
- private_subnet_ids
- isolated_subnet_ids

Optional "by AZ" outputs (if we can keep stable)
- public_subnet_ids_by_az (map(string))
- private_subnet_ids_by_az (map(string))
- isolated_subnet_ids_by_az (map(string))

Route tables (installer likely doesn’t need, but useful for debugging)
- public_route_table_ids
- private_route_table_ids
- isolated_route_table_ids

Egress
- nat_gateway_ids (list(string))
- nat_gateway_ids_by_az (map(string))

Validation rules (must-have)
- If create_vpc=true, vpc_cidr must be set.
- If enable_internet_gateway=true, public subnets must exist (created or provided).
- If nat_mode != none, private subnets must exist.
- CIDR overlap checks if creating subnets.
- If existing subnet IDs are provided, DO NOT also provide CIDRs for those tiers (or explicitly choose precedence and document).

Unresolved questions (vpc-baseline)
1) Do we support "isolated" tier in alpha, or keep it optional? Infra seems split; security likes it; support burden risk.
2) For "existing VPC" mode, do we require route tables to be managed by us? Current leaning: no; we just consume subnet IDs and assume connectivity is customer’s responsibility, but installer preflight will catch endpoint reachability.
3) Tagging standard exact keys: confirm w/ Irene/Victor. I’ve been using env/owner/cost_center/data_class placeholders.

---

Module: vpc-endpoints

Purpose
- Create required/optional gateway + interface endpoints and (optionally) enable private DNS.
- Align with ADR-0128.

Inputs (draft)
- vpc_id (string, required)
- region (string, required)

Subnets/security groups
- endpoint_subnet_ids (list(string), required)
  - Interface endpoints only.
  - Recommendation: use private subnets.
- endpoint_security_group_ids (list(string), required)
  - For interface endpoints.

Private DNS
- enable_private_dns (bool, default true)
  - Note: Some enterprises require this off due to central resolvers; we must document consequences (installer image pulls break if not resolvable).

Endpoint toggles
- create_s3_gateway_endpoint (bool, default true)
- create_ecr_api_endpoint (bool, default true)
- create_ecr_dkr_endpoint (bool, default true)
- create_cloudwatch_logs_endpoint (bool, default true)
- create_sts_endpoint (bool, default false)  (OPEN: may need to be true for "no public egress" installs; see oncall thread)
- create_ssm_endpoints (bool, default false)
  - For future; likely not required for installer.

Route tables for gateway endpoint
- gateway_endpoint_route_table_ids (list(string), required when create_s3_gateway_endpoint=true)
  - Expect private route tables at minimum.

Endpoint policies
- endpoint_policy_json_by_service (map(string), optional)
  - Key examples: "s3", "ecr.api", "ecr.dkr", "logs", "sts"
  - Default: AWS default (full access within VPC) unless Security wants stricter.

Outputs (draft)
- s3_gateway_endpoint_id
- interface_endpoint_ids (map(string))
  - Keys: ecr.api, ecr.dkr, logs, sts, ssm, ec2messages, ssmmessages
- interface_endpoint_dns_entries (map(string))
  - Useful for preflight / troubleshooting.
- private_dns_enabled (string or bool output)

Installer-facing outputs (explicit)
- required_endpoints_present (bool)
  - Only if we can compute reliably (might be tricky if endpoints optional). Could be a local check in examples instead.

Unresolved questions (vpc-endpoints)
1) STS endpoint default: should be true when nat_mode=none? Pilot issues suggest yes, but some customers want to use regional STS over egress allowlist; depends on model.
2) Endpoint policy defaults: Security likely wants at least "deny * except required actions" patterns, but that becomes heavy support. Maybe policy stubs + doc guidance for enterprise hardened variant.
3) Private DNS toggle: if enable_private_dns=false, should we output explicit DNS names customers need to configure in their resolvers?

---

Module: security-groups-baseline

Purpose
- Provide least-privilege SGs for common Redwood Private components and endpoints.
- There’s a risk we overfit to implementation details; ensure output names are stable and allow overrides.

Inputs (draft)
- vpc_id (string, required)
- allowed_admin_cidrs (list(string), default [])
  - For break-glass / bastion use cases. Ideally empty by default.
- allow_egress_to_internet (bool, default false)
  - If false, egress is restricted to VPC CIDR (and optionally prefix lists for AWS services? TBD).
- vpc_cidr (string, required)
  - Used to scope internal traffic.

Optional ports / component flags (alpha scope)
- enable_control_plane_sg (bool, default true)
- enable_data_plane_sg (bool, default true)
- enable_endpoint_sg (bool, default true)

Port sets (placeholders; verify with Ethan/Benji)
- control_plane_ingress_ports (list(number), default [443])
- data_plane_ingress_ports (list(number), default [443])
  - NOTE: This is very likely wrong for actual components; treat as placeholder until installer contracts are confirmed.

Outputs (draft)
- endpoint_security_group_id
- control_plane_security_group_id
- data_plane_security_group_id

Security posture notes
- Default should be: no 0.0.0.0/0 ingress.
- Egress default: either all egress allowed (common AWS default) OR restricted. Security prefers restricted; support prefers allow. We need a decision from Marcus + Infra.

Unresolved questions (security-groups)
1) What are the actual port requirements by component for alpha? We should avoid baking in ports if they might change.
2) Do we include any NACL opinionation? Current leaning from security thread: no NACLs in alpha; provide guidance only.

---

Module: redwood-private-vpc (wrapper)

Purpose
- Compose vpc-baseline + endpoints + sg-baseline for the "golden path".
- Provide a stable outputs contract specifically for installer.

Inputs (draft)
- name_prefix, env, tags
- region
- availability_zones
- vpc_cidr
- nat_mode (none|single|per_az)  (alpha: likely allow none/single/per_az only)
- enable_private_dns (bool)

Wrapper outputs (installer contract v0)
- vpc_id
- private_subnet_ids
- endpoint_subnet_ids (probably same as private_subnet_ids)
- endpoint_security_group_ids (list(string))
- interface_endpoint_ids (map(string))
- s3_gateway_endpoint_id

Installer mapping (notes)
- Proposed installer config expects:
  - network.vpc_id
  - network.subnet_ids (data plane)
  - network.endpoint_subnet_ids
  - network.endpoint_sg_id
  - network.endpoints.ecr_api_id, ecr_dkr_id, logs_id (and maybe sts_id)
  - network.endpoints.s3_gateway_id
- Need Ethan/Benji to confirm exact keys and whether they want list or map outputs.

---

Versioning and backward compatibility (quick notes)
- Outputs consumed by installer must be treated as "semi-stable" even in alpha.
- Any output rename = breaking for installer integration. If we must rename, provide old output as alias for >=1 minor version.
- Introduce explicit output contract doc once we settle on names.

---

Next steps / TODO
- [ ] Confirm required endpoint list for alpha (ADR-0128 alignment): ECR api/dkr, S3 gateway, CloudWatch Logs, STS?
- [ ] Get installer team to sign off on installer-facing output names (Ethan/Benji).
- [ ] Decide default egress posture in SG module (Marcus + Infra).
- [ ] Decide whether flow logs are owned by vpc-baseline vs separate module (Allison input).
- [ ] Write a minimal tfvars example using wrapper module and annotate which values are required.

Questions to bring to ENG-4821 review
- Are we okay having both (a) wrapper module contract and (b) lower-level modules with more granular outputs? This may increase surface area.
- For existing VPC mode: do we require customers to pass in both subnet IDs and route table IDs (for S3 gateway endpoint)? If they don’t want us touching route tables, we can’t create S3 gateway endpoint.
- Should we allow "private endpoints only, no egress" as a first-class topology in alpha? If yes, STS endpoint default likely flips to true.

Changelog (informal)
- 2025-02-19: Added explicit gateway_endpoint_route_table_ids requirement; added STS endpoint question; clarified wrapper outputs as installer contract.
- 2025-02-11: First pass at module split and naming conventions.
- 2025-01-29: Initial doc stub created for ENG-4821 kickoff.
